docs.title: AI-Powered Browser Memory Assistant
docs.text:
MemoryLane is an AI-powered browser memory assistant that allows users to search and retrieve webpages they have previously visited using natural language queries.

The system acts as an intelligent memory layer over browsing activity, helping users rediscover useful information without remembering exact URLs or keywords.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Modern users consume large amounts of information online but often struggle to find previously visited webpages, articles, documentation, and resources.

Traditional browser history only stores URLs and titles, making retrieval difficult.

MemoryLane solves this by understanding the meaning of previously viewed content.

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
MemoryLane aims to:

  • Store previously visited webpages
  • Understand webpage content using AI
  • Enable semantic search using natural language
  • Retrieve relevant browsing memories

docs.title: Browser Extension
docs.text: The Chrome extension automatically captures webpage information during browsing.

docs.title: Content Extraction
docs.text: Webpage content is cleaned and processed to remove unnecessary information.

docs.title: AI Summarization
docs.text: AI models generate summaries of stored webpages.

docs.title: Semantic Search
docs.text:
Users can search memories using natural language queries.

Example:

"Find documentation about ROS navigation"

docs.title: Memory Dashboard
docs.text:
The web application provides:

  • Search interface
  • Browsing timeline
  • Stored memories
  • Categories and tags

docs.title: User Authentication
docs.text: Users can securely manage their personal browsing memories.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Users frequently consume information online but struggle to retrieve it later.

Students, developers, researchers, and professionals often read useful resources but forget:

  • Website names
  • URLs
  • Exact keywords
  • Where the information was found

docs.title: Browser History
docs.text: Browser history requires users to remember website names or keywords.

docs.title: Search Engines
docs.text: Search engines retrieve information from the internet, not from the user's personal browsing history.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
MemoryLane creates an AI-powered memory layer over browsing activity.

Instead of searching using exact keywords, users can describe what they remember.

Example:

"Find that article about reinforcement learning I read last week"

MemoryLane retrieves the relevant webpage.
